headline: Approved January 21, 2026 meeting minutes unanimously and reviewed finance and housing project updates.
summary: The Trust approved the minutes from its January 21, 2026 meeting. Staff gave a finance report showing a Trust account balance of $1,558,295.79, and provided updates on the Inclusionary Zoning study, the Office of Housing Stability, and several affordable housing development projects including 213 Main Street, 245 Bryant Street, 272-274 Cross Street, Overlook Ridge 13B, and 105 Salem Street.
decisions: Approved the minutes from the January 21, 2026 meeting unanimously.

1. Call to Order 
Mayor Christenson called the meeting to order at 5:01 PM. 
 
Mayor Christenson presented the following remote meeting notice into the record: 
 
On March 28, 2025, Governor Maura Healey signed legislation extending certain 
COVID-19 relief measures including extending remote meetings for public bodies.  The 
same provisions which permitted multiple-member bodies to meet remotely, or convene in 
a hybrid manner, have been extended through June 30, 2027.  This extension allows 
public bodies to continue to meet remotely or to meet in a hybrid manner, without a 
quorum of the public body physically present at a meeting location, as long as the public 
body provides "adequate, alternative" means of access to remote meetings. This meeting 
will be conducted via remote participation. This meeting will not include in-person 
attendance by members of the public, but all effort will be made to permit public 
attendance, in the manner specified below, via remote access by internet, and telephone. 
Public access will also be provided by posting draft minutes, and/or a transcript, 
recording, or record of the meeting on the City of Malden website at cityofmalden.org as 
soon as practicable after the meeting.   
 
Additional information/guidelines for the public can be found here: 
https://www.mass.gov/service-details/updatedguidance-on-holding-meetings-pursuant-to-

2. Approval of Meeting Minutes from January 21, 2026 
On a motion by Ms. Angie Liou, seconded by Mr. Brian Slater, the minutes from the 
January 21, 2026 meeting were approved unanimously. 
 
3. Finance Report 
Mr. Grover delivers the finance report. The current Trust account balance is 
$1,558,295.79, inclusive of January interest in the amount of $3,985.62. The regularly 
reported expenses are January salary-related expenses of $200.00 applied, there will be 
additional expense-related items posted upon receipt of details. No operating expenses 
have currently encumbered. Current interest rate is 300bps or 3.00%; it was 3.25 static 
for the last 5 months. We can anticipate roughly $46.5k in interest per annum or 
$3,900.00 a month at 3.00. We are still participating in the Eastern Bank IntraFi Cash 
Service or Sweep agreement with Eastern Bank to mitigate risk and extract yield. 
Approved funding recommendations from Oct 2023, Feb 2025, Nov 2025 meetings 
respectively yet to be spent: $373,625.11 for 213 Main Street, $349,166.52 for Overlook 
Ridge 13B, and 400,000.00 for 105 Salem Street. This amounts to a total of 
$1,122,791.63. There are $435,504.16 in net funds available. 
4. Administrative Updates 
a. Inclusionary Zoning Economic Feasibility Study 
Mr. Gately provides an upcoming on the upcoming Inclusionary Zoning (IZ) 
Study and Economic Feasibility Analysis. Mr. Gately explains that it has been 
five years since the initial adoption of the City’s IZ ordinance, and that the City is 
interested in revisiting the ordinance to see what it can do to streamline future 
residential developments, without slowing market-rate development and 
incentivizing more affordable development. The City had sent out an RFQ for an 
IZ study and economic feasibility analysis and had received one response from 
RKG Associates. Mr. Gately adds that there is a contract out to RKG and are 
awaiting a response. Councillor Linehan asks a question if the City has a sense on 
how the current IZ ordinance has affected development. Mr. Gately responds that 
due to there not being any inclusionary units that have come online since the 
adoption of the ordinance, the City will revisit the ordinance to see how to 
improve. Councillor Linehan follows up and asks if there will be a public-facing 
aspect to this study. Mr. Gately responds that while the study itself won’t involve 
public engagement, there will most likely be options for public feedback upon the 
publishing of the study. 
            
5. Affordable Housing Program Updates 
a. Mayor’s Office of Housing Stability 
Mr. Gately provides an update on OHS. The Malden Office of Housing Stability 
has continued to help city residents looking for housing services, legal assistance, 
and general help with anything related to housing. They served 139 households

last quarter. Ms. Liou asks a question related to how this figure compares to that 
of previous quarters. Mr. Gately adds that this is typical for the past few quarters, 
with the previous two serving 176 and 147 households, respectively. Mr. Grover 
adds that the City will be partnering with the Lawyers Clearinghouse, a Boston-
based nonprofit that serves low-income clients, specifically as it relates to their 
tax-title. He adds that they do have a number of properties that go into tax 
settlement, and the clearinghouse does offer pro bono services for income-
qualified residents. He wanted to add this, as he feels that this is a good segway 
from OHS discussions. 
Mayor Christenson adds that the OHS contract ending at the end of the fiscal 
year, due to ARPA funds expiring. He adds that the City is trying to figure out a 
way to continue the services offered and has convened a group of surrounding 
communities to see if a regional approach is feasible. He continues to share a 
success story related to OHS in helping a resident pay back-rent in order to move 
into an available housing authority unit. 
b. Development Projects 
i. Existing Projects 
1. 213 Main Street (Asian Community Development Corporation) 
Ms. Angie Liou recuses herself for this update. ACDC has selected a 
general contractor and is on track to close on the project by mid-2026. 
Mr. Gately adds that the funding commitment for this project expires at 
the end of March, and the board will be voting to extend the 
commitment during their next meeting. 
2. 245 Bryant Street (Asian Community Development Corporation) 
ACDC received an update regarding its pre-application for 
CommonWealth Builder funds. The project was not invited into the full 
round, and the City is awaiting next steps regarding the project. 
3. 272-274 Cross Street (The Neighborhood Developers) 
Ms. Liou rejoined the meeting. The first two units have closed, one of 
which was filled by a Malden resident. One of the units is on track to 
close in the next couple of days. The remaining two units have had 
some difficulty in finding a buyer for a variety of reasons, including 
eligibility and obtaining financing. The realtor is continuing to work 
through the lottery list to fill the remaining units. There will be a 
resident-welcoming in the early-spring. 
4. Overlook Ridge 13B (WinnDevelopment) 
This project submitted a funding application to the State during their 
mini funding round and they were notified that they were not receiving 
funding. This project also has a funding commitment expiring at the 
end of March, and the board will be voting to extend the commitment 
during their next meeting.  
5. 105 Salem Street (Volunteers of America of Massachusetts) 
This project submitted their application to EOHLC for supportive 
services funds. They expect to be funded in full and have been working 
to secure other necessary project financing.
